solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dropping lead to investigate sea doing … possibly this?

definitions.text: Dropping lead to investigate sea doing … possibly this?

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so a letter leaves the fodder
the lead of a word is its first letter, which here is the one dropped
possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the remaining letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of investigate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what a sea creature is doing as it sinks out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I from SEA DOING and rearrange the rest to get SONDAGE. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a sondage is a sounding, and sounding the sea is investigating it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sondage is a trial trench or sounding, the kind of probe made when investigating what lies below the surface.

clue.text: Moustache’s trimmed, not so much hairy bristle?

indicators.note: trimming cuts parts away, and the word not tells us exactly which letters go
hairy in its slang sense of wild or alarming suggests letters thrown into disorder

blocks.note: read as one word, with the apostrophe ignored
taken as written; these are the letters that come out

explanation.surface: A man wonders if trimming his moustache will leave it less hairy and more bristly.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, O, M, U, C and H from MOUSTACHES and the letters T, A, E, S are left to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Seta is the biological term for a stiff hair on an insect, worm or plant, which is a bristle.

clue.text: Madonna regularly snubbed? That’s bad for such a versatile entertainer (10, two words)

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept
bad suggests letters gone wrong and out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
the second, fourth and sixth letters of snubbed

explanation.surface: A pop star is snubbed, and someone grumbles that this is bad news for a versatile performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man band plays several instruments at once single-handed, the very model of a versatile street performer.

clue.text: Shellfish lands almost on bottom of ocean

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off
in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of ocean
acres are areas of land

explanation.surface: Seafood ends up beached on the land after drifting from the ocean floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives nacre as mother-of-pearl and also as the shellfish that yields it, a rare sense found mainly in barred puzzles.

clue.text: Rocky edge eroded round banks of Rhône

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one piece wraps the other
a river's banks are its two sides, so the outside letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: something eroded has been eaten away
the first and last letters of Rhône

explanation.surface: A rocky ridge has been worn away beside the River Rhône in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: An arête is a sharp, narrow mountain ridge between glacial valleys, the knife-edge of rock climbers cross.

clue.text: Cavorting idly I get cold

indicators.note: cavorting is prancing about, so the letters jump into new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lazing about outdoors complains that they are catching a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelidity is the noun from gelid, meaning icy or frozen, so it names extreme coldness.

clue.text: 1000 pounds a year cover for head

blocks.note: a kip is an engineering unit of weight equal to 1000 pounds
per annum, Latin for a year

explanation.surface: Someone pays a thousand pounds a year for insurance cover for their head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 1000 pounds as money; it is a weight, the kip.
explanation.definitionFit: A kippa is the skullcap worn by Jewish men, a small covering for the crown of the head.

clue.text: Exercise sequences were in session hinging on spirit

indicators.note: something hinging swings back on itself, so the word flips direction

blocks.note: the ka is the spirit or soul in ancient Egyptian belief
a court or committee sat when it was in session

explanation.surface: A meeting was held whose outcome depended on the team's spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Katas are set routines of movements practised in karate and other martial arts, choreographed drills for training.

clue.text: Russian channel is carrying bitter articles

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the word is wraps around the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
tart means sharp or sour in taste
the plural of the article A

explanation.surface: A Russian broadcaster runs sharply critical pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: ITAR-TASS was the Russian state news agency, a major official channel for information out of Moscow.

clue.text: A sauce going round with rice dish

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so these letters face the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
sauce and lip both mean cheeky talk
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A sauce is passed round the table to go with a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce looks like a culinary word, matching the rice dish, but it means impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaw is a variant spelling of pilaf, the Middle Eastern dish of rice cooked in stock with spices.

clue.text: Guardian’s joke rebuffed LA citizen

indicators.note: rebuffed means sent back, so the word is turned around

blocks.note: a guardian angel
as in 'have you heard the one about…'

explanation.surface: A newspaper's attempt at humour falls flat with a reader from Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: Guardian invites the British newspaper; here it is a protective spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a native or resident of Los Angeles, the local demonym for its people.

clue.text: Revised grade (not D) got in a competitive exam

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter named
revised means reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student's revised mark, no longer a D, got them through a tough exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The agrégation is the highly selective French state examination for recruiting senior teachers and professors.

clue.text: Dachshund, bloodhound and kelpie ignoring confusion

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out of the reckoning

blocks.note: a bloodhound is slang for a detective, shortened to tec
taken as written
pie is a printer's word for jumbled type, hence confusion

explanation.surface: A list of dog breeds that seems to have muddled itself together.
explanation.walkthrough: The breeds all look like definitions; bloodhound is a detective, and kelpie only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Teckel is the German name, also used in English, for the long-bodied short-legged sausage dog.

clue.text: Block isolating Yankee prisoner?

indicators.note: isolating something sets it apart, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: to stay is to check or stop
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an old lag is a long-term convict

explanation.surface: A prison block keeps an American captive apart from the others.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the thing itself: a camp in which American prisoners of war were held apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for enlisted men in the Second World War, such as the famous Stalag 17.

clue.text: Academy’s imaginative accepting insensitive person’s “sorry”

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for academy
imaginative in the way verse is
a log is a person as unfeeling as a lump of wood

explanation.surface: An arts college's creative staff take in a tactless person who then apologises.
explanation.definitionFit: Apologetic means expressing regret, the adjective for someone who says they are contrite.

clue.text: Stream ritual showing baptismal ceremony

indicators.note: showing means putting on display, here letters visible inside the phrase

blocks.note: the tail of the first word joined to the head of the second

explanation.surface: A ritual by a river shows a baptism taking place.
explanation.definitionFit: Amrit is the sweetened holy water used in the Sikh initiation rite, and by extension that ceremony itself.

clue.text: I start to get about part of Sussex waterway

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of get
A is an abbreviation for about
the rapes were the six old administrative divisions of Sussex, an English county

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to explore a stretch of Sussex by its waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: Part of Sussex looks like an instruction to take some letters from the word; it is the old county division called a rape.
explanation.definitionFit: An igarapé is a narrow channel or creek in the Amazon basin, navigable by canoe.

clue.text: Question variable ten to one ratio

indicators.note: something variable can change, so the letters take another order

blocks.note: QU is an abbreviation for question
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks about changeable odds of ten to one.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten to one sounds like betting odds, which fits the ratio, but the words are only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotient is the result of dividing one number by another, so it expresses a ratio between them.

clue.text: Film covering port gathering to turn round ship

blocks.note: a bee is a social gathering, as in a sewing bee
a ship at anchor swings when it turns with the tide

explanation.surface: A camera crew films around the harbour as a ship turns.
explanation.walkthrough: Film and port suggest movies and harbours; they are a skin forming on the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeswing is the filmy crust of tartar that forms in old port and other long-kept wines.

clue.text: Bottled lime drunk with a spot of effervescent mineral

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order
a spot is a tiny amount, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the four letters of lime, rearranged
bottled and lit are both slang for drunk
the first letter of effervescent

explanation.surface: A fizzy lime drink served in a bottle gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottled and drunk both seem to describe the lime drink; one means intoxicated, the other mixes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Melilite is a group of silicate minerals found in volcanic rocks, typically yellowish crystals.

clue.text: Preposterous Beeb broadcast with nil value

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A viewer fumes that a BBC programme was worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is a nickname for the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster, which makes broadcast look like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbelievable means too absurd to be credited, just as something preposterous defies reason.

clue.text: Be hit with Noel’s cost around beginning of January — giving this?

definitions.text: Be hit with Noel’s cost around beginning of January — giving this?

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so its letters are scattered
the beginning of a word is its first letter
around means surrounding, so the shuffled letters enclose the single one

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
the first letter of January

explanation.surface: The bills for Christmas arrive in early January, teaching someone a hard lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel is Christmas, so the whole clue pictures the January shock of festive spending as a practical warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a vivid practical example that teaches something, here the pain of overspending.

clue.text: Bill fellow extra charge

blocks.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man named Bill is charged extra.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, or an invoice to match the charge; it is an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is something supplementary tacked onto a basic price, such as an optional surcharge.

clue.text: Sad Elon Musk oddly rocks around Tesla

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions
rocks means shakes back and forth, so the letters are jumbled
around means encircling, so the jumbled letters enclose another

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A tech billionaire is gloomy as his car company is rocked by trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker; it is the scientific unit, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesto is an Italian musical direction meaning mournful, telling the player to perform in a melancholy way.

clue.text: Kind hereditary factor embodying mother’s or father’s side?

indicators.note: embodying means holding within, so one piece sits inside the other
a word's side is one of its edges, here the end letter shared by both words

blocks.note: a gene is the unit of heredity
both words end in the same letter

explanation.surface: A trait might be inherited from either the maternal or the paternal line.
explanation.definitionFit: Genre means a sort or category, especially of artistic work, which is what kind means as a noun.

clue.text: When entering nobleman denied opening decree

indicators.note: denied its opening means the first letter is taken away
entering means going inside, so this word sits within the other

blocks.note: a duke is a high-ranking nobleman
as in 'as the day ended'

explanation.surface: A nobleman refused entry when he arrived issues a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict of the Russian tsar, and by extension any arbitrary official order.

clue.text: Day sharing cool spring sojourn

indicators.note: sharing a space means sitting between the others, so this letter goes inside

blocks.note: in means fashionable
D is the abbreviation for day
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Someone spends a day at a cool spa on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To indwell is to live or abide within a place, the same as staying there for a while.

clue.text: European slalomer maybe avoiding top of icy ridge

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping it out, so that letter goes
the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a slalomer is one kind of skier, hence maybe
the first letter of icy

explanation.surface: A Continental skier swerves around the top of a frozen ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An esker is a long winding ridge of gravel left by a stream under a melting glacier.

clue.text: Robbed once match official’s heading for tunnel

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: short for referee
the first letter of tunnel

explanation.surface: A football fan complains of being robbed as the referee heads for the players' tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: Once marks an archaic word: reft is an old past tense of reave.
explanation.definitionFit: Reft is the archaic past participle of reave, to plunder or deprive, so it meant bereft or robbed.

clue.text: Dished out grass for feed

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grass was served up as fodder for the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddish is a dialect word for aftermath, the second growth of grass after mowing, used for grazing livestock.

clue.text: Batman delivering one-two, ie in action, POW!?

indicators.note: delivering means letting go, and the one-two means the first two letters
in action means moving about, so the letters change positions

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic-book fight scene: the superhero lands a one-two punch, and the caption reads POW!
explanation.walkthrough: POW looks like the sound effect from the Batman comics; it is the abbreviation for prisoner of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner of war is held in a camp, and an inmate is anyone confined in such an institution.

clue.text: Time off to catch fish? Start off with one fish

definitions.note: the clue word is read as a plural, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: the first off means taken away, so that letter is removed
the second off means out of order or gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to net is to catch fish
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler takes a fishing holiday and starts by landing a single fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Time off reads as a holiday; it is an instruction to remove the time letter. The word off then does a second job as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon tetras are small bright blue-and-red South American freshwater fish, very popular in home aquariums.

clue.text: Edge back from disco dance …

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a tang is a projecting point or prong, such as the tongue of a blade
the last letter of disco

explanation.surface: Someone edges back away from the disco floor as the dancing starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina, performed by couples with sharp, dramatic movements.

clue.text: … again choose dance therapy of a sort

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, dancing is prescribed as a kind of therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect is to vote someone into the same office a second time, picking them once more.
